title: 【2026上海迪士尼攻略】不買快速通關也能刷完！門票/必玩設施/親子實戰心得
text:
【2026上海迪士尼攻略】不買快速通關也能刷完！門票/必玩設施/親子實戰心得
 由 
 V妞的旅行
 ·
 已發表 1 10 月, 2026
 · 已更新 6 10 月, 2026
2026上海迪士尼最新攻略！玩上海迪士尼，除了課金購買快速通關（尊享卡），其實「選對入園日子」搭配「時間差玩法」，就算只持一般門票也能玩完熱門大項。這篇攻略統整最新入園政策、門票選法、尊享卡（快速通關）精算、親子推車動線與必吃美食，並收錄 V 妞多次實地造訪的現場實測心得，幫大家避開排隊人潮，順暢玩遍各大經典與最新設施！
【V妞30秒行前速懂精華】
關鍵證件：台灣旅客購票與現場入園必須備妥台胞證正本（護照無法查驗）。
最高回報投資：加購「樂園早享卡」，開園前提早 1 小時入場直奔《瘋狂動物城：熱力追蹤》，省下 2–3 小時排隊。
入園動線順序：先通過行李安檢（嚴禁自熱食品、野營推車）→ 刷台胞證與拍照檢票 → 進入米奇大街。
APP 關鍵操作：一刷過閘門，立刻打開「上海迪士尼度假區 App」掃描全家門票並搶領免費預約卡。

為什麼一定要去上海迪士尼？
上海迪士尼樂園擁有全球最大迪士尼城堡「奇幻童話城堡」，園區巧妙融入東方文化元素（如十二朋友園），更擁有全球首座《動物方城市》（瘋狂動物城）主題園區。
全球最大奇幻童話城堡：宏偉氣派，內部設有皇家宴會廳、晶彩奇航水上體驗與多重互動項目。
全球首座《動物方城市》主題園區：1:1 還原大都會場景，搭乘「熱力追蹤」展開沉浸式追捕。
全球首發創極速光輪（TRON）：趴騎式光輪摩托車，感受未來科幻彈射的極速快感。
全新園區進度：度假區第九大主題園區「蜘蛛人主題園區（毗鄰瘋狂動物城）」各項乘騎設備已進入最後測試階段，高科技漫威遊樂設施即將登場！
👉 預訂優惠：[上海迪士尼優惠門票]｜[迪士尼尊享卡（快速通關）]｜[樂園早享卡（提早入園）]
上海迪士尼-V妞的遊玩小秘訣
去過這麼多次迪士尼，上海這座「全球最大城堡」真的每次去都有新發現！為了讓大家的夢幻旅程不踩雷，V妞特別整理了幾個私房筆記：
拍照黃金位不只有城堡正前方：正門人潮永遠最多，V妞心得：推薦走到「奇想花園」側邊小徑或石橋旁，能拍到城堡與湖水倒影同框的畫面，完全不用跟後方遊客互卡。
推車辨識超重要：帶小朋友入園，門口即可租借官方單人推車；若自備推車，需符合長 110cm、寬 80cm 以內的規範（禁止露營拉車）。V妞心得：各熱門設施外都有專屬推車停放區，工作人員常因巡遊動線調整移動推車位置，強烈建議在推車把手綁上亮色絲巾或顯眼掛飾，離場才能秒認。
自備大容量行動電源：進園後整天都要依賴官方 App 查看排隊時間、抽預約卡、掃碼入場，耗電量極大。V妞體驗：雖然園區有共享行動電源，但熱門時段常遇到機台全空或無槽可還，自己帶一顆大容量行動電源最踏實。
善用單人通道（Single Rider）：如果同行家人或朋友願意分開乘坐，「創極速光輪」與「雷鳴山漂流」有時會開放單人通道，排隊時間通常只要常規通道的一半。
精簡隨身包加速安檢：入園是「先安檢、後檢票」。工作人員會逐一檢查隨身包包，請勿攜帶需加熱加工的食品（如泡麵、自熱鍋）或玻璃容器；隨身行李越精簡，通過安檢與刷證入園的速度就越快。
煙火散場的撤退動線：看完夜間煙火秀後若要搭乘地鐵或叫車，建議稍微加快腳步往出口移動，可避開散場瞬間擠爆地鐵 11 號線與西公交樞紐計程車站的人潮高峰。
上海迪士尼日期挑選心法：人少才是最高 CP 值
上海迪士尼園區廣闊，排隊時間隨淡旺季落差極大。若想避開人潮、免買高價尊享卡也能玩得盡興，日期的選擇至關重要：
黃金大淡季推薦：
元宵節後至 3 月初：農曆春節人潮退去後的空窗期，入園人數大幅下降。雖然氣溫偏低（白天約 10 度上下），但排隊體感極佳，熱門設施甚至能輕鬆二刷。
11 月至 12 月中旬（聖誕節前）：避開萬聖節與年底大假，且週二至週四是一週內人潮最少的時段。
排隊落差：淡季平日的現場等候時間，官方 App 顯示 50 分鐘時，實際常常 35–40 分鐘就能玩到；若在暑假或連假前來，動輒 90–120 分鐘起跳。
上海迪士尼門票與實名制規範
購買上海迪士尼門票與加購快速通行，必須注意官方嚴格的實名查驗制度：
台灣旅客購票必讀（實名制關鍵）：
證件限制：購買門票時，護照號碼不適用。台灣旅客必須輸入《台灣居民來往大陸通行證》（台胞證）號碼。
實體證件查驗：入園當天必須攜帶台胞證實體正本，於檢票閘門刷證拍照核驗身分。
同行人同行進場：同一筆訂單綁定的所有同行者，入園時必須全員到齊，並由主訂人持證件一同核銷進場。若同行親友抵達時間不同，建議分開下單購買。

門票與提早入園怎麼選？
決定玩 1 天還是 2 天：園區範圍極大，帶幼童的家庭推推車步調較慢，建議選擇 2 日票 免去趕場壓力；年輕朋友若體力充沛，可選 1 日票搭配早享卡。
加購「樂園早享卡」（提早入園）：早享卡可比正式開門時間提早最多 1 小時從專屬通道進場。
V妞心得：早享卡是這趟行程最划算的投資！入園後直奔最熱門的《瘋狂動物城：熱力追蹤》，排隊不到 20 分鐘就能玩到，接著順路走去明日世界玩「創極速光輪」，直接省下現場動輒 3 小時的排隊時間。
上海迪士尼尊享卡（快速通關）與預約等候卡精算
上海迪士尼的快速通行官方名稱為「迪士尼尊享卡」（Disney Premier Access，簡稱 DPA）。如果你不想把大半天的時間耗在排隊動線中，尊享卡就是最高效的解方，直接走專屬快速通道入場。
尊享卡分為「單項購買」與「多項套裝方案」，涵蓋從 3 項到 15 項的全套暢玩組合，可依照停留時間與同行成員需求靈活挑選：

註：尊享卡價格採浮動制，平旺季與連假期間價格會有所調整，實際價格請以預訂當日系統顯示為準。
熱門尊享卡方案細項解析
單項設施尊享卡：適合想把預算花在刀口上的朋友。例如：清晨先利用普通通道或早享卡玩完「熱力追蹤」，下午人潮高峰時再單獨加購 1 張「翱翔·飛越地平線」，兼顧時間與荷包。
3 項設施套裝（5 大組合）：
冒險套票 A：創極速光輪、雷鳴山漂流、巴斯光年星際營救
冒險套票 B：七個小矮人礦山車、抱抱龍沖天賽車、古蹟探索營繩索挑戰道
暢玩組合：翱翔·飛越地平線、小飛俠天空奇遇、小熊維尼歷險記
娛樂演出套裝：米奇奇想花園見面會、冰雪奇緣歡唱盛會、米奇妙遊童話書
6 項設施套裝（2 大組合）：
6 項探險套裝：瘋狂動物城：熱力追蹤、創極速光輪、雷鳴山漂流、七個小矮人礦山車、巴斯光年星際營救、古蹟探索營繩索挑戰道。
6 項暢玩套裝：瘋狂動物城：熱力追蹤、加勒比海盜—沉落寶藏之戰、翱翔·飛越地平線、晶彩奇航、巴斯光年星際營救、小飛象。
8 項設施套裝（全園最熱門首選）：涵蓋瘋狂動物城：熱力追蹤、翱翔·飛越地平線、創極速光輪、雷鳴山漂流、加勒比海盜—沉落寶藏之戰、七個小矮人礦山車、晶彩奇航、巴斯光年星際營救。
15 項尊享套裝（全日暢玩無痛攻頂）：包含全園熱門遊樂設施，並享有日間巡遊（米奇童話專列）與夜間煙火秀（奇夢之光幻影秀）的專屬保留觀賞位，不用提早 1 小時坐在地上卡位。
尊享卡使用流程與注意事項
綁定門票：通過檢票閘門入園後，打開官方「上海迪士尼度假區 App」掃描門票 QR 碼完成綁定。
選擇時段：在 App 內檢視已購買的尊享卡項目，確認各設施的預約通行時段。
掃碼入場：依預約時間抵達設施入口處，向工作人員出示 App 內的尊享卡 QR 碼即可走快速通道進場（每項設施限用 1 次）。
注意事項：
每日數量有限：熱門設施與套裝在旺季常於上午迅速售罄，強烈建議提早線上預訂。
限當日單次有效：尊享卡逾期即失效，不可跨日使用或轉讓。
時段綁定需留意：部分熱門項目（尤其是表演及巡遊專屬位）有嚴格的入場時間窗口，錯過即無法補用，排行程時各設施間要預留 20–30 分鐘步行時間。
尊享卡怎麼選最划算？
只想玩特定 1–2 個大項 ➔ 早享卡 + 單項尊享卡（提早進園刷熱力追蹤，下午課金買飛越地平線，CP 值最高）。
想兼顧刺激與熱門 ➔ 6 項探險套裝 或 8 項暢玩套票（適合體力充沛的一日遊旅客）。
攜帶長輩或幼童同行 ➔ 3 項暢玩組合 / 演出套裝（避開高強度排隊，輕鬆看秀與溫和型遊樂設施）。
預算充足、追求零排隊 ➔ 15 項全套暢玩（煙火巡遊免提早卡位，直接享有最佳視野）。

免費「迪士尼預約等候卡」
特定日期園區會啟用免費線上排隊功能。入園刷過閘門、門票綁定 App 後，即可在首頁搶領。
適用項目：米奇妙遊童話書、風暴來臨：傑克船長之驚天特技大冒險、冰雪奇緣：歡唱盛會等熱門劇場演出。
搶卡技巧：同時間只能持有一張預約卡，演出體驗結束後才能預約下一場。熱門室內劇場建議一進園立刻領取第一場次。
上海迪士尼開放時間
上海迪士尼的每日營運時間會依淡旺季與平假日動態調整，並非全年固定。出發前 1–3 天務必打開官方 App 確認當日最新時刻表：
常規營運時間：通常為 08:30 開園 – 21:30 閉園（淡季平日有時為 09:00 – 21:00；暑假或連假旺季可能提早至 08:00 開園、延至 22:00 閉園）。
早享卡入場時間：比當日官方公告的正式開門時間提早整整 1 小時（例如 08:30 正式開園，早享卡 07:30 即可由專屬通道安檢進場）。
重要演出參考時段（每日時間依 App 公告為準）：
日間巡遊（米奇童話專列）：通常於中午 12:15 與下午 15:45 各有一場。
夜間煙火秀（奇夢之光幻影秀）：通常於閉園前安排 1–2 場（常見為 20:00 與 21:15）。若當晚有兩場，推薦看第二場，人潮明顯分散許多。
V妞體驗：現場安檢閘門通常會比官方表定時間再提早 15–20 分鐘開始疏導排隊人流。如果沒有買早享卡，強烈建議在正式開園時間前 60–75 分鐘抵達檢票廣場排隊，才能在第一時間衝進去玩到第一項設施！
上海迪士尼樂園地圖
上海迪士尼樂園佔地極廣，是以中央「奇幻童話城堡」與「奇想花園」為中心，向外輻射出各大主題園區。目前樂園常態營運為 8 大主題園區（另有興建中的漫威蜘蛛人主題園區）：
米奇大街（迎賓入口）：入園第一站，集合各大周邊紀念品旗艦店與角色互動合照點。
奇想花園（核心樞紐）：位於城堡正前方，包含旋轉木馬與「晶彩奇航」，也是觀賞夜間城堡煙火秀的正面黃金區。
瘋狂動物城（全園最熱門）：全球首座動物方城市，必玩無軌道警車追捕設施「熱力追蹤」。
明日世界（科技速度感）：科幻霓虹風格，擁有全球首發的趴騎式「創極速光輪」與「巴斯光年星際營救」。
夢幻世界（童話經典）：城堡後方腹地最大的區域，代表作是溫和刺激的「七個小矮人礦山車」與適合親子的「小飛俠天空奇遇」。
寶藏灣（海盜冒險）：全球唯一海盜主題區，沉浸感封神的「加勒比海盜：沉落寶藏之戰」就在這裡。
探險島（神秘遠古）：排隊大戶「翱翔·飛越地平線」與清涼激流「雷鳴山漂流」的所在地。
迪士尼·皮克斯玩具總動員：巨型玩具視角，必玩擺盪彈射的「抱抱龍沖天賽車」。
V妞動線心得： 園區走一圈動輒 15,000–20,000 步，最忌諱東奔西跑「折返跑」。
早享卡衝刺路線（順時針）：清晨利用早享卡直衝最深處的「瘋狂動物城（熱力追蹤）」➔ 順路往右切入「明日世界（創極速光輪）」➔ 接著往「夢幻世界」順時針推進，能在前兩小時無痛刷完兩大排隊魔王。
一般門票家庭路線（逆時針）：若開園才進場，動物城與明日世界早已大排長龍，建議改走逆時針玩法：先往左直奔「探險島」或「寶藏灣」，趁大家都在右側時搶先玩加勒比海盜，把熱力追蹤留到傍晚人潮稍微分流時再去，玩起來最省力！
上海迪士尼必玩設施
上海迪士尼園區廣大、項目繁多，如果時間或快速通關（尊享卡）預算有限，絕對不能亂槍打鳥。推薦策略是「先鎖定全園 5 大必玩設施」，接著依照同行夥伴（幼童、長輩、刺激控）從「分齡族群推薦」中穿插安排，玩起來最有感、最不虛此行！
TOP 1：熱力追蹤（動物方城市）
位置：瘋狂動物城
身高限制：無身高限制
排隊方式：常規排隊、尊享卡
特色：採用先進的無軌道騎乘系統，坐上警車跟著茱蒂與尼克在冰川鎮、撒哈拉廣場穿梭追捕壞人。
V妞心得：排隊動線本身就是景點！沿途經過警察局大廳、豹警官辦公桌、監獄走廊，每個細節都極度逼真。整座主題園區連紅綠燈與不同體型動物的專屬設施都做出來了，拍照非常殺底片。設施轉彎與加減速非常流暢，大小朋友都能玩得極為投入。
TOP 2： 創極速光輪（TRON）
位置：明日世界
身高限制：122 公分或以上
排隊方式：常規排隊、尊享卡、單人通道
特色：騎乘重型摩托車姿態彈射出發，結合高對比度霓虹燈光與電音節奏。
V妞心得：衝刺與下墜的離心力非常強烈，趴著騎的視角讓速度感加倍放大。設施提供隨身物品小置物格（僅限眼鏡、手機），大包包需要先在入口旁免費寄物櫃刷門票 QR 碼寄放。
V妞體驗：如果不害怕刺激感，推薦傍晚或天黑後再坐一次，戶外軌道穿過藍橘霓虹穹頂的瞬間，夜景視野與科幻氛圍遠勝白天！
TOP 3：加勒比海盜：沉落寶藏之戰
所在園區：寶藏灣
身高限制：無身高限制
排隊方式：常規排隊、尊享卡
亮點特色：巨幅曲面巨幕投影結合實景水面特效與爆破，船體會旋轉、倒退與下沉，視覺震撼力堪稱全球迪士尼暗黑騎乘設施的頂峰。
V妞心得：這項設施是全園區科技水準的代表作之一，巨型球幕和水上特效結合得天衣無縫，水下浮出巨大幽靈船與傑克船長現身的瞬間極具視覺衝擊力。排隊消化速度相對快，即使排隊長度顯示 40 分鐘，動線也走得十分流暢，屬於全齡必玩項目。
TOP 4：翱翔·飛越地平線
所在園區：探險島
身高限制：102 公分或以上
排隊方式：常規排隊、尊享卡
亮點特色：懸掛式座椅升至半空，搭配 IMAX 球幕帶你俯瞰全球名勝，附帶微風與草地、海風香氣特效。
V妞體驗：這項設施全天候排隊時間都居高不下（動輒 80–120 分鐘）。如果沒有買尊享卡，建議安排在午餐或日間遊行時段前往，排隊時間會稍微縮短。
TOP 5：七個小矮人礦山車
所在園區：夢幻世界
身高限制：97 公分或以上
排隊方式：常規排隊、尊享卡
亮點特色：溫和型雲霄飛車，車廂會隨著軌道轉彎自然左右搖擺，穿梭在發光寶石礦洞中。
V妞心得：適合剛滿 97 公分、想嘗試刺激的小朋友。節奏流暢且不暈眩，礦坑內的小矮人和發光寶石場景做得很精緻，是全家都能同樂的雲霄飛車首選。
 親子幼童友善設施推薦（溫和無負擔、低身高門檻）
帶著幼童或長輩同行，若不想挑戰高離心力設施，這些項目排隊體感相對輕鬆、故事氛圍溫馨，最適合闔家同樂：
小飛俠天空奇遇（夢幻世界／無身高限制）：
搭上懸吊式海盜飛行船俯瞰倫敦夜空，穿梭在夢幻島星空中，視覺細緻柔美，幼童接受度極高。
小熊維尼歷險記（夢幻世界／無身高限制）：
乘坐蜜蜂罐小車進入百畝森林，色彩繽紛溫馨，完全無刺激感，是小小朋友的最愛。
巴斯光年星際營救（明日世界／無身高限制）：
坐上移動巡邏車，拿起雷射槍瞄準 Z 字標靶射擊積分。互動感十足且室內冷氣充足，排隊時間通常較短，非常適合親子組隊競賽。
小飛象（奇想花園／無身高限制）
可自行操控手柄升降的小飛象座艙，在高空可飽覽城堡與奇想花園綠地，步調悠閒放鬆。
大朋友刺激挑戰推薦（離心力與戶外冒險設施）
如果是年輕朋友同行、熱愛重力加速與失重感的冒險控，在刷完創極速光輪後，絕不能錯過以下挑戰：
抱抱龍沖天賽車（玩具總動員／身高限制 120cm）：
U 型橘色軌道高速來回擺盪俯衝。刺激度介於七個小矮人與創極速光輪之間，失重感相當強烈，喜愛小刺激但不敢挑戰極速光輪的

title: 上海豫园游玩攻略：藏在老上海的江南园林与城市烟火，领会中式浪漫
text:
上海豫园游玩攻略：藏在老上海的江南园林与城市烟火，领会中式浪漫
有鱼
更新于 2026/07/03
上海豫园游玩攻略来袭！豫园藏在上海的黄浦老城厢里，拥有着不一样的园林风格。它历经数百年修缮，完整保留传统造园布局与明清古建风貌。园内山水相依、景致层次丰富，九曲桥、玉玲珑等景观极具特色。既有着清幽的园林环境，又衔接着热闹的老城街巷。
藏在上海黄浦老城厢里的豫园，将雅致山水、百年古建、满目绿意与鲜活市井烟火完美交织，告别了都市快节奏的紧绷与匆忙。漫步园内，三穗堂、万花楼等明清古建错落有致，一步一景都是江南里的诗意。一转身，便是烟火街巷，古雅园林与老城烟火撞个满怀。既有中式园林的婉转古韵，又有老上海独有的松弛温柔。如果想要解锁上海慢生活、拍出氛围感大片的话，请看这份上海豫园游玩攻略吧！
上海的标志性景观在哪里？
如果你来到上海旅游一定会很好奇上海的标志性景观在哪里？
那便是黄浦区老城厢核心位置的上海豫园，这里有着江南极具代表性的古典园林，也是上海本土极具辨识度的老牌人文地标。多数游客来上海，只会奔赴外滩江景、陆家嘴高楼，却不知道能真正代表老上海本色、承载城市本土记忆的核心去处，其实在老城厢这片区域。
上海豫园有哪些特点？
豫园最突出的特点就是兼具了古典园林的静谧和老城街巷的热闹。园内是清幽舒适的园林景致，园外衔接老城厢街区，商铺密集、美食众多、常年人流不断，两种氛围相互交融，造就了上海独一份的游玩体验。
初次来上海怎么游豫园？
不管是初次来沪的外地游客，还是多次到访、想深度游玩城市的本地人，豫园都是值得慢走细看的地方。这里没有新式景区过度商业化的浮夸感，满是岁月沉淀的城市质感和生活气息，能让人真切触摸到老上海最原始的生活模样。在豫园能清晰感受到这种独特的反差，园区步道平缓好走，游玩节奏完全可以自主把控，不用扎堆拥挤。随处找廊下、窗边驻足停留，都能安静放空，随手拍照也能避开大量路人，氛围感十足。
上海豫园历史介绍
豫园始建于明代，历经数百年岁月变迁和多次保护性修缮，完整保留了最初的园林结构和景观布局。区别于其他现代仿造园林，豫园的整体框架、建筑排布、山水走势，全部延续古代造园的原始规划，是上海为数不多原汁原味留存至今的古典园林遗存。
豫园游玩体验
整座园林规模适中，不会因面积过大导致走路疲惫，也不会因体量过小导致观赏内容单薄。古人精心规划园区格局，区域划分清晰、景观分布均匀，行走观赏的体验极佳，充分展现了江南传统造园工艺的成熟水准。
慢悠悠走完整个园区耗时刚刚好，全程轻松不费力，老人小孩都能适配。近距离观察园内的建筑砖瓦、木质结构，能清晰看到岁月留下的痕迹，和全新仿造的园林质感完全不同。沉浸式闲逛的过程中，能真切体会百年古园的沉稳质感。
豫园风景与造园核心
豫园的造园核心，依托自然山水打造，是江南园林最经典的造园思路。园区将古建房屋、天然池水、原生绿植自然融合，没有刻意的人工堆砌痕迹，所有景观顺着地势自然排布，整体观感柔和协调。
园内绿植品类丰富，包含各类乔木、灌木和草本植物，四季景观各有特色。春天草木新生、满眼清新，夏天绿树成荫、全园清凉，秋天枝叶变色、氛围温柔，冬天枝干利落、景致素雅。一年四季风景各不相同，任何时段前来游玩，都能收获全新观感。
豫园游玩体验
山水相依的布局让园林充满灵气，静态的古建搭配流动的池水和鲜活的草木，动静结合、层次丰富，全程逛下来轻松耐看，不会出现审美疲劳的情况。
夏季游玩体感格外舒适，大面积树荫遮挡阳光，园内温度明显低于室外街道，全程不用暴晒。湖边常有微风拂面，逛累了在水边驻足，身心都能得到放松。四季景致差异直观，每次前来都有新看点，重复游玩也不会觉得单调乏味。
如何体验上海豫园里的中国美？
含蓄的中国美
豫园的造园风格主打简约自然，摒弃繁杂花哨的装饰，空间布局和自然的景观搭配完美，展现中式园林独有的中国含蓄美，是江南古典园林的经典样式。园内所有古建均承袭明清建造风格，随处可见的飞檐、回廊、雕花窗格、实木梁柱，园内建筑不会孤立突兀，而是和周边的山水池水、花草草木完美适配，形成完整的景观体系。
临水建筑贴合水景视野，山间亭台适配山林氛围，沿路回廊衔接游览动线，每一处设计都贴合整体环境，完美诠释中式造园的协调美学。豫园里满满都是中式美学，如果不理解，欢迎联系我，为你安排一位专业导游，带你沉浸式逛豫园。
 联系客服定制行程
豫园游玩体验
即便不懂园林美学，也能直观感受到这里的景致舒服规整，干净不杂乱。园内的雕花窗格、木质梁柱细节精致，慢慢驻足细看，能发现很多手工打造的独特细节。随便找一处点位拍照，画面干净雅致，不用刻意找角度，轻松拍出古风氛围感大片。
豫园园林风光
豫园的景观层次丰富饱满，整体排布有序规整，核心景观突出、次要景致点缀到位，没有杂乱堆砌，顺着原有地势打造景观，不强行改造地貌，最大程度保留自然原生形态。游客缓步游览，每转过一处拐角、走过一段回廊、跨过一座小桥，眼前景致都会焕然一新，不同视角能看到完全不同的园林风光。
豫园游玩体验
豫园最出彩的游玩亮点就是移步换景，全程游览新鲜感十足。不用刻意寻找打卡点，每一次转弯都能遇见新风景，彻底避免一眼望穿的单调感。边走边停、拍照观赏的节奏十分惬意，不管是快速闲逛还是深度慢游，都能拥有很好的体验。
豫园人气最高的景点
九曲桥和湖心亭是豫园人气最高、最具代表性的核心打卡点，地处园区观景最优位置，视野开阔、视角绝佳，是游园必逛的核心区域。两处景致依水而建，相辅相成，构成豫园最经典的水景画面。
九曲桥
九曲桥桥面曲折绵延、顺着水面自然延伸，行走节奏舒缓平缓，没有赶路的压迫感。站在桥面可以近距离观赏湖面水波、岸边绿植和临水古建，全方位欣赏园林水景，也是拍摄氛围感照片的绝佳机位。
湖心亭
湖心亭静静伫立在湖边，造型简约朴素，和周边水景绿植完美融合。这里是天然的休憩区域，逛园疲惫时可以在此驻足停留、吹风歇脚，沉浸式感受园林的松弛氛围，有效舒缓游玩的疲惫感。
玉玲珑
镇园奇石玉玲珑坐落于园林核心位置，是豫园的标志性自然人文景观。奇石历经数百年风吹雨打，孔洞天然、纹理细腻，自带厚重的岁月气息。这一处独特的奇石景致，大幅提升了整座园林的文化质感和观赏价值。
九曲桥一定要缓步慢行，每一处弯折的观景视角都不相同，出片率极高。湖心亭非常适合中途休整，静坐吹风看湖景，解压效果十足。近距离观赏玉玲珑，能直观感受江南赏石文化的独特魅力，核心景致打卡体验饱满充实。
上海豫园古建筑观赏推荐
豫园保存着大规模、高完整度的明清古建群落，涵盖厅堂、阁楼、亭台、廊道、院落等多种建筑类型，品类齐全、保存完好，是上海地区十分珍贵的古建实景群落。
三穗堂
三穗堂气势庄重，作为豫园极具分量的主厅，承载着丰收吉祥的美好寓意，也见证了旧时市井商聚、文人雅集的热闹过往，一梁一柱皆是岁月沉淀的厚重底蕴。
老君殿
老君殿清幽古朴，飞檐翘角间藏着淡淡的古韵禅意，古旧木构与精巧雕花历经时光洗礼，自带一份宁静悠远的氛围感。
涵碧楼
涵碧楼临水而立，凭栏便可揽一池碧波，水光与楼阁相映成趣，清风拂面，尽显江南临水建筑独有的温柔诗意。
和熙堂
和熙堂温润雅致，依偎在山水花木之间，通透的格局藏着闲适安然的意境，于闹市之中守得一方静谧，惬意又治愈。
万花楼
万花楼精巧秀丽，楼阁雅致、花木环绕，每一处细节都尽显匠心。正对着玉玲珑，光影流转间，把江南园林的灵动浪漫演绎得淋漓尽致。漫步其间，目之所及皆是古韵风华，一步一景，都让人沉醉在这份跨越百年的东方诗意里。

豫园灯会
豫园每年最出圈的民俗一定是豫园灯会，也是上海的年度重头戏。一到夜晚，满园灯火通通点亮，古色古香的楼阁被彩灯环绕，光影闪闪、氛围感十足。各式各样的主题花灯好看又热闹，年味满满，不管是本地人还是外地游客，都会特意来打卡。

title: The Bund, Shanghai: Maps, How to Visit, and What to See
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
The Bund, Shanghai: Maps, How to Visit, and What to See
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Aug. 31, 2026 
The Bund is Shanghai's most iconic landmark, and if it's your first visit, give yourself 2–3 hours if you want both the historic buildings and the skyline; 30–60 minutes is enough for a quick photo stop.
For the classic night scene, arrive before sunset and watch the city lights come on gradually, enjoying the sharp contrast between day and night. 
If you value open space and a calmer pace over close-up detail, the North Bund offers a quieter skyline view, but you'll miss some of the intimate Bund atmosphere.
Main Bund or North Bund: Which One Should You Choose?
The Main Bund and the North Bund offer two very different ways to experience Shanghai's waterfront.
For most first-time visitors, we recommend the Main Bund.
The Main Bund is the famous stretch along Zhongshan East 1st Road, where you walk beside Shanghai's historic waterfront buildings — the architectural collection often referred to as the "Museum of World Architecture." Across the Huangpu River is the Pudong skyline.
The North Bund sits further north, around the Huangpu River and Suzhou Creek. It gives you more space, fewer people, and wider views back toward both Pudong and the historic Bund.
So the choice is simple:
Choose the Main Bund if you want to get close to Shanghai's historic buildings and understand the stories behind them.
Choose the North Bund if photography, open space, and skyline views matter more to you than architectural history.
5-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou and Suzhou Explore the Elegant China
Main Bund Cultural Walk: Our Top Choice for First-Time Visitors
The Bund
Time needed: 2–3 hours
Best for: First-time visitors, history and architecture lovers, families, and couples
If this is your first time in Shanghai, this is the route we recommend.
The Main Bund is not just about standing by the river and taking the classic skyline photo. The real experience is in the buildings behind you.
Along this stretch are Shanghai's famous historic waterfront buildings, built in dramatically different architectural styles. But unless you know what you are looking at, it is easy to walk past them without understanding why they matter.
Our route: Former Astor House area → Garden Bridge → Peace Hotel → former HSBC Building → Bund waterfront
On our private walking tour, we don't just point at the buildings from the street. Depending on opening hours and access arrangements, we can take you inside selected historic buildings and explain the stories behind them.
You will see how this part of Shanghai developed during the 1920s and 1930s, when the city became one of Asia's most international trading centers, and how foreign banks, hotels, and trading companies shaped the architecture that still defines the Bund today.
At the same time, you still get the classic view across the Huangpu River toward Pudong's modern skyline.
This is the best route if you want to understand why the Bund is important, rather than simply take a photo of it. And that is how we design the rest of our Shanghai tours too — not simply taking you to see the city, but helping you experience it and understand the stories behind it.
9-Day Beijing ,Xian and Shanghai Tour China Family Classic Tour 
North Bund Walk: Better for Space and Photography
Shanghai North Bund with Little Egg
Time needed: 1.5–2 hours
Best for: Photographers, repeat visitors, and travelers who prefer fewer crowds
The North Bund is where we would send you if you have already seen the Main Bund — or if you care more about photography than getting close to the historic buildings.
The waterfront here is more open, with fewer crowds and more room to walk.
You also get several different angles for photographing the Pudong skyline, the historic Bund buildings, and the Huangpu River. Instead of walking directly among the historic architecture, you are looking back toward it from a greater distance.
That makes the North Bund a better choice if your priority is wide skyline shots rather than architectural details and historical stories.
It can also be a smart alternative during extremely busy travel periods, such as the Labour Day holiday or National Day Golden Week, when the Main Bund can become particularly crowded.
Our route: Shanghai Postal Museum → Garden Bridge → North Bund waterfront → Little Egg → riverside viewpoints
This is a looser walk built around viewpoints rather than a historical narrative. You can stop where the views interest you rather than following a strict sightseeing sequence.
However, for most first-time visitors, we still would not choose the North Bund instead of the Main Bund.
You may get more space and more photo opportunities, but you lose the chance to walk directly among the buildings that made the Bund famous.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
When Is the Best Time to Visit the Bund?
Arrive Around 2 PM: Get the Full Bund Experience (Most Recommended)
In-depth tour of the Bund in Shanghai
This is our top recommendation if you are visiting the Bund for the first time.
This gives you enough daylight to see the historic buildings properly, rather than viewing them only as illuminated facades at night. You can spend around 2.5 hours on an in-depth walk, then take a break for afternoon tea before returning to the waterfront as the sky begins to change.
By staying until after sunset, you get both sides of the Bund in one visit: the architectural details and stories that are easiest to appreciate during the day, followed by the Pudong skyline as the lights gradually come on.
Arrive 30–60 Minutes Before Sunset: Best for the Skyline Night View
Watching the sunset on the Bund in Shanghai
If the Pudong skyline is all you really want to see, there is no need to spend the entire afternoon at the Bund.
Arrive around 30–60 minutes before sunset and stay until the city lights are fully on.
The advantage is not just seeing Shanghai at night. You get to watch the scene change from daylight to dusk, then to a fully illuminated skyline. This transition is what creates the dramatic contrast behind many of the Bund's most recognizable views.
As a rough guide, sunset is usually around 6:30–7:00 PM in summer and 5:00–5:30 PM in winter, although the exact time changes throughout the year.
If you arrive only after dark, the view is still impressive — but you will miss the transition.
Go Around 8:30 AM on a Weekday: Best for Avoiding Crowds
On a weekday morning, the Bund in Shanghai is sparsely populated.
Around 8:30 AM on a weekday, traffic is light, the promenade is nearly empty, and you can walk or jog along the river with almost no one around.
However, most historic buildings won't be open yet, so you may need to wait half an hour to an hour before embarking cultural walking tour, or you want the exterior views and a quiet atmosphere.

title: Jade Buddha Temple, Shanghai: What to See and How to Visit
text:
Home
 Destinations

Jade Buddha Temple, Shanghai: What to See and How to Visit
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Sep. 24, 2026 
Jade Buddha Temple was built around 1918 in the style of the Song Dynasty (960-1279). Named for its 1.9-meter-high white jade Buddha, Jade Buddha Temple is worth about 1–1.5 hours if you want to see the temple's most prized treasure and experience an active Buddhist temple.
If you are on a tight schedule, or your priority is the Bund, Shanghai's old neighborhoods, or the city's modern skyline, you can skip it.
Visit it if you want:
to see Shanghai's famous jade Buddhas;
to experience an active Buddhist temple;
to learn more about Chinese Buddhist culture;
or to spend some time with traditional temple architecture.
Skip it if you want:
Shanghai's skyline and modern cityscape;
old neighborhoods and cafés;
or a very short list of the city's highest-priority sights.
What to See Inside Jade Buddha Temple
Jade Buddha Temple
Address: 170 Anyuan Road, Putuo District, Shanghai
Opening hours: 8:00–16:30 on regular days
Admission: Free
Metro: Line 13, Jiangning Road Station, Exit 3
Walk from the station: About 5 minutes
Recommended visit: 1–1.5 hours
1. The Two Jade Buddhas: The Absolute Must-see
The white jade Buddha of Jade Buddha Temple
The temple is named after two white jade Buddhas brought to Shanghai from Myanmar in the late 19th century.
The most important stop is the Jade Buddha Hall, where you can see the seated jade Buddha, about 1.9 meters high. Then continue to the Reclining Buddha Hall to see the smaller reclining jade Buddha, which represents the Buddha before entering nirvana.
If you only have one hour, prioritize these two halls. You don't need to inspect every hall or Buddhist statue to understand why the temple is significant.
2. Traditional Chinese Temple Architecture
Roof decorations of the Jade Buddha Temple
The jade Buddhas are the main attraction, but the temple itself is also worth noticing.
As you walk through the complex, look for the symmetrical layout, yellow walls, traditional rooflines, courtyards, and carved decorative details.
The architecture gives you a very different side of Shanghai from the skyscrapers around the Bund and Lujiazui.
If you enjoy Chinese architecture, allow a little extra time to walk rather than rushing directly from one Buddha hall to the next.
Photography Tips
If you want photos, focus on the architecture, courtyards, roof details, and overall temple atmosphere rather than trying to photograph every hall.
Photography is restricted in certain worship areas or during religious activities. Follow the signs inside the temple.
3. Taste the Vegetarian Cuisine
The temple also has a vegetarian food section serving traditional Buddhist vegetarian dishes with Shanghai-style cooking (priced at 50–70 RMB per person).
This works well for vegans, or if you want to eat immediately after visiting rather than finding another restaurant.
I would treat the vegetarian food as an optional add-on, not the main reason to visit. Come for the jade Buddhas first.
Check detailed information on its official website: Jade Buddha Temple.
5-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou and Suzhou Explore the Elegant China
How Much Time Do You Need at Jade Buddha Temple?
Koi Pond at the Jade Buddha Temple
Less than 1 hour: See the two jade Buddhas, look around the main halls, and leave.
1–2 hours: See the two Buddhas, explore the main architectural spaces, and spend some time observing the temple atmosphere. This is the amount of time we would suggest for most travelers.
2–3 hours: Worth considering if you have a strong interest in Buddhism, Chinese temple architecture, religious culture, or an interest in having a vegan meal inside.
If you are visiting Shanghai for only one or two days and Buddhist culture is not a priority, don't force Jade Buddha Temple into your itinerary simply because it is famous.
The time may be better spent on the Bund, the Former French Concession, or another experience that matches your interests more closely.
If you're unsure whether it deserves a place in your short Shanghai itinerary, tell us how many days you have and what else you want to see. We can help you decide where it fits without adding unnecessary cross-city travel.
8-Day Beijing–Xi'an–Shanghai Tour China Golden Triangle
Jade Buddha Temple vs. Jing'an Temple: Which Fits Your Itinerary?
Shanghai Jing'an Temple night view

Choose Jing'an Temple for a quick architectural stop, while opting for Jade Buddha Temple if you want to spend more time understanding Buddhist culture and seeing the famous jade Buddhas.
You don't need to visit both unless temples are a specific interest.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
How to Fit Jade Buddha Temple into Your Shanghai Itinerary
Jade Buddha Temple works best as one stop within a Former French Concession route, rather than as a destination that requires a special trip across Shanghai.
For example, you could visit the Former French Concession in the morning, have lunch nearby, and then continue to Jade Buddha Temple for a cultural immersion.
If your Shanghai itinerary is already full, don't add the temple just to collect another famous attraction.
If you want to visit Jade Buddha Temple without wasting time crossing Shanghai, we can build it into your private sightseeing route and combine it with nearby experiences that match your interests.

text:

Best/Worst Times to Visit Shanghai 2026: Tips for All Months
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Apr. 13, 2026 
We're often asked when the best time is to visit Shanghai.
Shanghai has a humid subtropical climate with four distinct seasons, and there's something to enjoy anytime you visit.
The simplest answer: autumn (September to November) is sunny, mild, and dry, and relatively uncrowded. Spring (March to May) is also lovely, though a bit more humid with occasional light rain.
But if you want to avoid the crowds or catch a specific seasonal highlight, a general "best season" answer isn't always enough.
Based on our experience and customer feedback, we've found that timing your trip around specific periods can make a big difference. We'll share those insights below, so you can plan a vacation that's as close to perfect as possible.
Considering your stay in Shanghai may not be too long, you may also want to know how to plan a Shanghai trip that meets your needs and travel length.
Content Preview
Autumn and Spring: Top Choices
Winter: The Cheapest Time
Summer: The Worst Time Without Strategies
Dates to Avoid in 2026/2027
Autumn and Spring: Your Top Choices
Wukang Mansion in Autumn, Shanghai, China
Autumn (September to November) is the best season to travel to Shanghai. 
Summer crowds, the rainy season, and heatwaves begin to fade, prices return to normal, and the weather is perfect for leisurely city walks.
For more stable weather, plan your trip for later than mid-September, and check the forecast before you go. Typhoons can affect Shanghai from July to September, but the probability drops sharply after mid-September.
Beyond weather, if you're hoping to see Shanghai's autumn colors, aim for mid-November to mid-December. Due to global warming, this cooler window has become a more reliable time for foliage.

Cherry blossoms in full bloom at Guyi Garden in Shanghai in spring
Spring (March to May) is also a great time to visit Shanghai, offering pleasant days around 15°C (59°F) but more light rains (9 rainy days vs. 6 rainy days) compared to autumn.
If you want to experience the traditional Chinese ink painting-like beauty of the water towns, March and April are the best months to visit.
Early to mid-March can be relatively cold, so if you're sensitive to the cold, consider visiting after mid-March.
Late March to early April is the cherry blossom season, where you can enjoy great scenery at spots like Hongkou Football Stadium and Gucun Park.

Shanghai Weather in March
Shanghai Weather in April
Shanghai Weather in May
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
Winter: The Cheapest Time
Lantern Festival at Shanghai City God Temple
Winter (December to February) in Shanghai is cold and damp. It rarely sees snow and mainly experiences rain.
Despite the cold, winter offers two big advantages: costs are generally about 30% lower than normal, and crowds are the thinnest of the year—except around late December (Christmas and New Year celebrations) and early February (Chinese New Year).
Aim for December if winter is your only option, when it is a festive month and the days are not that cold, which means you may still witness Shanghai's beautiful foliage.
As for January and February, the coldest months, it is better to focus on indoor activities with heating, such as admiring ancient bronzes at the Shanghai Museum, marveling at the stunning Jade Buddha at the Jade Buddha Temple, and attending a cooking class in a traditional longtang home.

Summer: The Worst Time Without Strategies
Our clients are taking a boat tour in Zhujiajiao Water Town
Summer (June to August) is Shanghai's hottest, rainiest, and most typhoon-prone season, with average monthly rainfall of 5.2 inches and temperatures around 80°F (27°C).
Early to mid-June is your best window, when the temperatures and crowds haven't peaked yet, and rain is less frequent.
July is the hottest and most crowded month. Expect significant increases in hotel and airfare prices, as well as large crowds at attractions.
August is slightly cooler and less crowded than July, but typhoons are more likely and can affect flights. Be sure to check weather forecasts carefully and plan accordingly.
Travel with China Highlights

title: Shanghai Weather in January 2027: Tips for The Coldest Month
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Shanghai Weather in January 2027: Tips for The Coldest Month
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated May. 15, 2026 
January is Shanghai's coldest month, with average temperatures ranging from 2–8°C (36–46°F). Compared to December, January is slightly colder and has more rainy days average of 5–6 days, with a rainfall of 1.6 inches/41 mm.
The weather was usually cloudy and rather cold, but recent winters have been mild. You can tell that from 2026, which followed the 2025 warm-winter pattern, with daytime highs often above 6°C (43°F), and there were 10 rainy days with all light rain.
Is January a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Our clients experienced a boat tour at Tongli Water Town in Shanghai in January.
January may not be the best time to visit Shanghai, but it's still a nice month. 
As the coldest month of Shanghai, it's not bitterly cold, but it does feel damp and chilly, especially on overcast days.
Compared to the bustling Christmas and New Year celebrations in December and the lively Chinese Spring Festival in February, January is much quieter and offers a more affordable journey.
And if you want a true off-season experience without the holiday rush in 2027, aim for early to mid-January (January 1–20), as late January may coincide with the Chinese Spring Festival travel rush (February 5–11, 2027).
4-Day Shanghai Family Disneyland Tour 
What to See and Do in Shanghai in January
Experience New Year's Day Tradition: Height Climbing
Shanghai Tower's observation deck
If you have a habit of getting up early to exercise and aren't afraid of the morning chill, feel free to join locals in the Chinese custom of climbing to a high place for good luck in the new year on January 1st.
You can book your spot in advance for the Oriental Pearl Tower run, where you can run up to the 30th floor in 18 minutes and shout New Year's greetings to the whole of Shanghai.
It's okay if you don't want to participate in large events. Just head to the Shanghai Tower's observation deck for a leisurely stroll, and take in the panoramic view of Shanghai in the new year.
Stay Warm for Indoor Cultural Attractions
Most of Shanghai's top sights are indoors and heated.
If you are interested in Chinese aesthetics and history, the Shanghai Museum (East Campus) could be an excellent choice, where you can easily spend hours exploring bronzes, sculptures, and ancient paintings without feeling the cold.
For guests with Buddhist beliefs, the Jade Buddha Temple offers a tranquil spiritual retreat amidst the chanting and the sounds of wooden fish drums, and the temple's enclosed halls are quite comfortable.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
Stroll for New Year Sales in Shopping Malls
As the Chinese New Year approaches, shopping malls in Shanghai decorate according to the zodiac animal of the year, and locals flock to buy New Year's gifts and decorations.
This means you may find great sales and promotions, especially in mid-January. Just head over to the nearest large shopping mall, such as Xintiandi, Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, and IFC Mall in Pudong. 
Even if you don't buy anything, the festive window displays and red-gold decorations are a visual treat.
Warm Up by Enjoying Local Specialties
There's always a street food option at the night market that suits your taste.
Shanghainese cuisine has plenty of cold-weather comfort dishes.
For a local breakfast, try savory soy milk with fried dough sticks. And don't miss a bowl of glutinous rice wine soup (jiu niang yuanzi), which tastes sweet, warm, and slightly alcoholic, perfect for a chilly morning.
And you could not miss the xiaolongbao (soup dumplings) at Nanxiang Steamed Bun Restaurant (南翔馒头店). Its crab roe soup dumplings (蟹粉小笼包), dipped in ginger and vinegar, are a delightful blend of sweet and savory flavors, fragrant yet not greasy, leaving you feeling warm and cozy.
8-Day Zhangjiajie, Furong, Fenghuang, and Shanghai TourShanghai- Zhangjiajie - Furong - Fenghuang- Changsha 
What to Pack and Wear in Shanghai in January
Zhujiajiao Water Town, Shanghai
January's cold, damp weather calls for a focus on indoor activities and daytime outings. Evenings can be uncomfortably chilly, so plan to wrap up outdoor sightseeing by 5 PM.
Layering is your best strategy, normally a thermal base with a fleece or a thick sweater, plus a windproof coat or a down jacket to keep yourself warm. Choose water-resistant boots with thick socks on cold, rainy days.
Don't forget to bring a sturdy umbrella and a waterproof shell to layer over your coat. And a medium-sized backpack could also be useful, since most indoor spaces are heated, and you will want to hold your extra layers.
Visiting Shanghai in January with China Highlights
Most travelers come in spring or autumn, ignoring January also offers something they miss: true off-season peace, more affordable costs, and a rare chance to see the city at its most local.
The cold? Manageable with the right layers and a smart itinerary. Let China Highlights craft a winter escape that balances cozy indoor treasures with unforgettable daylight adventures.

title: Shanghai Weather in September 2026: Mild, Quieter, and Tips
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Shanghai Weather in September 2026: Mild, Quieter, and Tips
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Apr. 29, 2026 
Shanghai's September marks the beginning of autumn and sees the retreat of summer crowds.
September's average temperature ranges from 21°C (70 °F) to 27°C (81 °F), with an average of 8 rainy days having 3.9 inches (99 mm) of precipitation. 
Summer heat still lingers in early September, and it is normal to see temperatures reach over 35°C (95 °F). Data from September 2025 shows a peak of 38°C (100°F) on September 6th.
But you can expect a gradual drop from mid-September, by the end of September, to around 21°C (70 °F).
September is also the tail month of Shanghai's typhoon season. Though the peak time falls at late-July and late-August, you still need to try your luck and there is a possibility of encountering a typhoon.
Is September a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Our clients in Yu Garden in September, Shanghai
September is one of the best months to visit Shanghai. 
Rainfall decreases, crowds are much thinner than in July and August, queues at attractions are shorter or even nonexistent, and the weather begins to cool to a more comfortable level. 
But not all of September is the same. Choosing the right window within the month can make a real difference. Let me walk you through it.
1. Early September (1–10): Summer Heat Lingers, But Crowds Have Already Left
Early September still feels like summer. Daytime highs often reach 28–30°C (82–86°F), and in 2025, it was still usual to exceed 35°C (95°F), though humidity is noticeably lower than in August. 
The good news? Summer vacation is over. 
Most Chinese students are back in school, so tourist numbers drop sharply. You'll find shorter queues at popular spots like the Oriental Pearl Tower and Yu Garden. 
If you don't mind the lingering warmth, this is a great time for a quieter trip. Just plan outdoor activities for the morning or late afternoon, bring a handheld fan, and stay hydrated.
2. Mid-September (11–20): The Best Window with Mild Days and the Fewest Crowds
The French Concession, Shanghai
If your schedule is flexible, aim for mid-September. This is the window I recommend to our clients, friends, and family. 
Daytime temperatures average 24–27°C (75–81°F), with low humidity and gentle breezes. Evenings are cool enough for a long walk along the Bund or a night cruise on the Huangpu River.
Crowds are at their lowest of the month, and hotel rates are still reasonable. Whether you want to explore the French Concession, visit Zhujiajiao Water Town, or simply wander the city streets, this is the time to do it.
2-Week Shanghai, Suzhou, Hangzhou, Guilin, Xian, and Beijing Tour Touch Chinese Elegance 
3. Late September (21–30): Festivals Bring Back the Crowds
The Mid-Autumn Festival in 2026 falls on September 25–27. Many Chinese travelers take extra days off to extend the holiday with the following National Day holiday (October 1–7). 
Popular attractions get crowded again, and hotel prices begin to rise. If you're traveling in late September, book your flights, hotels, and attraction tickets at least 2–3 months in advance. 
Also, expect larger crowds, especially at family-friendly places like Shanghai Disneyland and Zhujiajiao. The weather remains pleasant, so with good planning, you can still have a wonderful time. >>Contact us to start planning your trip
4. Will I Be Affected by the Typhoon?
September is still within Shanghai's typhoon season (July to September). However, typhoons are much less frequent than in August. 
When they do occur, they usually happen in early September and pass within 1–3 days. By mid-September till the end, the risk is very low. 
So if you're traveling in early September, pay more attention to check the weather forecast a few days before departure and keep your itinerary flexible. A small buffer can save you from unexpected delays.
9-Day Beijing ,Xian and Shanghai Tour China Family Classic Tour 
What to See and Do in Shanghai in September
Citywalk in Shanghai: A Time-Travel Contrast
The night view of the Bund, Shanghai
September's mild weather is perfect for walking. I suggest two very different but equally fascinating routes.
The Bund: Witnessing the Fusion of History and Modernity
Start at the Bund. Walking along the Huangpu River and taking in the historic colonial buildings on the Puxi side, you will see that the architecture is from the 1920s and 1930s. 
Then turn around and look across the river. There stands Pudong's futuristic skyline: the Oriental Pearl Tower, Shanghai Tower, and Jin Mao Tower. It's a stunning contrast between old and new Shanghai, all in one view.
The French Concession: The Legendary Life of China's Godfather
Head to the French Concession, where we will take you through Du Yuesheng's life, who became a Chinese mob boss from a nameless.
Many will describe the French Concession as quiet and romantic. It is full of charm to wander through tree-lined streets and see trees forming a green shade overhead, adorning villas and secluded courtyards.
Stop at Basement FG Vintage, the predecessor of Sanxin Company that was founded by Huang Jinrong, Du Yuesheng, and Jin Tingsun. 
You may be hard to trigger by wandering through an ancient building, not until our guide tells you the story behind it, including its inextricable link to the opium trade in the French Concession of Shanghai.
Enjoy Shanghai's Parks and Wildlife: Strengthen Family Bonds
Shanghai Wild Animal Park
As crowds recede, September's comfortable days make it a great time to visit urban green spaces and wildlife attractions, especially suitable for multigenerational trips.
Shanghai Disneyland
You can expect shorter queues with pleasant weather during this period, and the park starts decorating for early autumn. 
If you want to fully experience the whole park within one day without two-hour waits, such as the Zootopia: Hot Pursuit or Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, this is your window.
Shanghai Wild Animal Park
Located in Pudong, this is one of China's best safari parks. You can take a feeding truck through the free-roaming animal zones and see lions, tigers, and bears up close. 
If Chengdu isn't on your itinerary, come here to see giant pandas. 11:30 AM and 2:30 PM are the pandas' "snack time," which is also the best time to observe them. At these times, the pandas will surround their keepers, begging for food, appearing exceptionally lively and adorable.
Shanghai Ocean Aquarium
Welcome to the only aquarium in the world with a dedicated China exhibit featuring Yangtze River basin species. Here, you'll see rare Chinese sturgeon, Yangtze alligators, and other native aquatic life. 
It's also one of the largest man-made seawater aquariums in the world, large enough for a family afternoon of exploration or a rainy backup plan during early September.
Experience Mid-Autumn Festival Traditions
Take a cooking class to learn how to make mooncakes
If you're in Shanghai during the Mid-Autumn Festival (September 25–27, 2026), we would like you to participate in the traditional activities rather than just watching.
We'd like to teach you how to make traditional Shanghai mooncakes (or soup dumplings (xiaolongbao) if you don't like mooncakes), and enjoy hairy crabs with chrysanthemum tea. 
After a satisfying meal, let's go to Yu Garden to enjoy the Mid-Autumn Festival lantern display, and admire the bright moon hanging in the sky together.

Shanghai Attractions
Shanghai, as the most modern international metropolis in China, boasts a wide variety of attractions that are scattered throughout the city. Foremost among them are the views along the Huangpu River, which divides Shanghai into two distinct worlds. The east bank presents a futuristic atmosphere because of numerous uniquely designed skyscrapers reshaping the urban skyline, with the highest one standing at an impressive 632 meters (2,073 feet). While on the west bank exudes a retro and historical charm, for there are rows of century-old European-style architectures along the Bund, retelling the stories of old Shanghai.
Moreover, Shanghai is home to the iconic traditional Chinese garden, Yu Garden; China’s most prosperous commercial street, Nanjing Road; and the most advanced Disneyland over the world, Shanghai Disneyland Park. If you fancy historical treasures, then don't miss the Shanghai Museum East. Wandering around the Zhujiajiao Ancient Town, you can experience the authentic local life and witness Shanghai’s tenderness. In short, there are always different appearances of the city waiting for your exploration.
Top Attractions
The Bund – Time-honored European Architectural Complex On the Bund along the west bank of Huangpu River, there stand a series of distinct and magnificent classical European-style architectural complexes, attracting millions of tourists every year. Over a century ago, they mushroomed as foreign-funded business and government offices, transforming this area into a bustling "Far East Wall Street". Now, most of them have become fashionable landmarks for high-end brand stores, luxury hotels, art galleries, restaurants, and leisure venues, standing opposite the modern skyscrapers across the river. When the lights ablaze at night, the entire Bund is dressed in a golden brilliant coat and the skyscrapers on the opposite riverbank also shine colorfully; the beautiful scenes on both sides are reflected on the Huangpu River, forming a stunning dazzling picture. At this time, taking a sightseeing boat and enjoying the charm of this night view while feeling the gentle breeze is the most pleasant experience.
Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street - the No. 1 Commercial Street in ChinaThe Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, known as "the No.1 Commercial Street in China", is one of the most bustling commercial streets in Shanghai. With the total length of approximately 1.5 kilometers (1,600 yards), it is a paradise for tourists to shop and enjoy delicious food. Strolling through it, you can witness how the contents of this commercial thoroughfare has seamlessly transitioned from international luxury brands to contemporary Chinese fashion, from daily necessities to high-end electronic products, and from century-old Shanghai delicacies to Michelin-starred cuisine. While you are drawn to the various shops, the pleasant tinkling sound will direct your attention to the distinctive sightseeing vehicle – the retro-style trolley. Riding on it, you can leisurely travel through this bustling street that combines both European classical elements and modern artistic atmosphere.
Yu Garden – Classical Chinese Garden in Shanghai DowntownYu Garden stands out among the modern buildings and bustling cityscape in Shanghai downtown. It was built over 450 years ago during the Ming Dynasty (1368 - 1644) and is one of the most renowned classical gardens in China. The garden features exquisite pavilions, rockeries, ponds, curved bridges, corridors, embossments, and carvings, showcasing the essence of traditional Chinese garden art. Among them the most interesting treasure is the Exquisite Jade Rock – it has a history of more than one thousand years, with a peculiar shape and dense small holes all over it, creating a mysterious atmosphere. Besides, the garden also preserves a large number of antique furniture and famous calligraphy and paintings as cultural relics from the Ming and Qing (1644 - 1911) dynasties.
Shanghai Museum East – Comprehensive Presentation of Chinese CivilizationShanghai Museum East has a comprehensive collection of Chinese ancient relics that not only cover all Chinese historical periods, but also feature extensive varieties ranging from bronzes, ceramics, jade, sculptures to calligraphy & paintings. The Great Bronze Cauldron, as one of the must-see artifacts, has mysterious animal patterns outside and eulogistic inscriptions inside, showcasing the superb craftsmanship of bronze forging existed over 3,000 years ago. Looking at the Sky Blue-glazed Plate manufactured more than a thousand years ago, you will be amazed how ancient Chinese managed to create such a smooth porcelain in vivid color without machines. Additionally, there is another branch, Shanghai Museum on People's Square, which now has transformed into a hub of world relics where you can admire exquisite antique Chinese furniture, diverse handicrafts from different Chinese ethnic minorities, as well as overseas cultural heritage such as the Olmec Colossal Stone Head and Greenstone Figures from Ancient civilizations of the Americas.
Zhujiajiao Water Town – Shanghai's VeniceZhujiajiao Ancient Town, about 1.5 hours’ drive away from Shanghai downtown, was built along the waterways and so is known as "Shanghai's Venice". The town has a history of over 1,700 years and preserves a great many architectural complexes from the Ming and Qing dynasties. Everywhere in the town are small bridges and flowing water, with white walls and black tiles decorating both sides. The whole water town presents a quaint and peaceful landscape of the typical Southern China style, contrasting sharply with the urban hustle and bustle of Shanghai. Tourists here can’t help but slow down and fully appreciate the beautiful scenery. At sunset, taking a traditional rowing boat to cruise and watching the red lanterns on both banks light up one after another would be an extremely enjoyable experience.
Shanghai Disneyland Park – Fairyland in RealityShanghai Disneyland Park, as the first Disneyland in Chinese mainland and the sixth in the world, is the newest and most modern one. Apart from the classic globally shared amusement areas and entertainment facilities such as Pirates of the Caribbean and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, it has also created a globally exclusive "Zootopia" themed area. The entire park uses high-precision projections and VR interactive technologies to bring the magical world from fairy tales to reality, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the game scenarios following the main characters in the animated films. Moreover, Shanghai Disneyland Park is filled with Chinese elements, such as the Tai Chi-wielding Donald Duck, Disney characters transformed into the twelve Chinese zodiac signs, and the integration of classic operas of Peking Opera in the musicals, providing you with a unique playing experience different from other Disneyland parks.
Shanghai Tower – the Tallest Skyscraper in ChinaShanghai Tower is situated on the east bank of the Huangpu River in Lujiazui. Standing at a height of 632 meters (2,073 feet), it ranks the tallest building in China and the third tallest in the world. The entire buil

1. Visa-free Policy for Traveling to Shanghai
Starting from November 30, 2024, citizens from 38 countries including France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Malaysia, Switzerland, Ireland, Hungary, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Australia and Japan can visit China, including Shanghai, without a visa and stay for up to 30 days. Currently, the number of countries that can travel to China without a visa has increased to 63.
Moreover, passport holders of 54 countries and regions including the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand enjoy a 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit when taking an international transfer via Pudong International Airport (PVG), Hongqiao International Airport (SHA), and international cruise ports in Shanghai.
Cruise passengers from all foreign countries can enjoy a 15-day Visa-Free Policy for Cruise Tour Groups to Shanghai if they meet all the requirements. Pudong, Shanghai 
2. Must-see Attractions in Shanghai
The Bund, as the landmark of Shanghai, is a must-see for travelers going there. On in, there is a cluster of western style buildings erected in the 1920s and 1930s. Benefiting from their different styles, they are called “expo of world buildings”. Opposite the Bund across the Huangpu River, is a totally different skyline with skyscrapers standing one by one including the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower, and World Financial Center. What’s more, it’s recommended to spend time appreciating Shanghai’s other beauties, covering Nanjing Road, Yu Garden, Disneyland Park, Yuyuan Bazaar, Jade Buddha Temple, Zhujiajiao, Waibaidu Bridge, Longhua Pagoda, Old Street, etc.
See More About:  Shanghai Attractions
3. Common Payments Methods in Shanghai
In Shanghai, there are several common payment methods:
a. Alipay and WeChat Pay:
Alipay and WeChat Pay are the most commonly used payment methods in Shanghai now, covering almost all consumption scenarios. So, how to pay via WeChat or Alipay?
1). Use your mobile phone to download and install the WeChat or Alipay APP, register according to the APP instructions, and enter your mobile phone number and other information.
2). Open the app and bind an international bank card with the logos of Mastercard, Visa, JCB, Diners Club, Discover, etc. 
3). When paying, open the APP and scan the merchant's payment QR code or show your payment QR code to the merchant.
b. Credit cards:
In some large supermarkets and hotels, you can choose to pay directly by swiping your VISA or MasterCard.
c. Cash:
Of course, cash payment is also an available option. You have the convenience of exchanging Chinese yuan at the airport or withdrawing it from any ATM that is affiliated with the bank of your card.
4. Universities and International Schools in Shanghai
 Kindergarten Shanghai has several prestigious universities, including Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Fudan University, and many international schools, offering excellent education at all stages for students. 5. A Converter May be Necessary.
The standard voltage in China is 220V, 50 Hz. A majority of sockets are dedicated to flat double sockets or flat triple sockets. Most hotels provide converters for their guests. But just in case, packing a converter should be on the “What to do before going to Shanghai” list, or travelers can buy one from electronic stores in Shanghai.
6. Squat Toilets in Public Areas and Western Toilets in Hotels
Most public toilets are squat toilets; but a few western toilets can be found as well, like in shopping malls, scenic spots, and airports. Some places will have the prompt to inform which type of toilet it is. The toilets in hotels mainly are western toilets. Remember to carry toilet tissues for most public toilets do not provide them.
7. Free Wi-Fi is Widely Available.
The coverage of free wireless networks is extensive, and you can easily connect WIFI freely in your hotel, shopping mall, airport, scenic spots, coffee shops, restaurants, and other public areas. But sometimes the Internet speed is relatively slow, not so satisfactory.
8. Medical Services
Shanghai offers excellent medical conditions. Specifically for international patients, there are dedicated international hospitals like Shanghai Jiahui International Hospital and Shanghai United Family Hospitals and Clinics. These hospitals possess professional and amiable medical teams that offer top-notch services and guarantee seamless communication with patients from various countries. Moreover, they can interface with your insurance to safeguard your rights. The medical environment is also pleasant, allowing you to feel relaxed during the treatment process.

The Bund Shanghai
 The Bund, the landmark of Shanghai, is a 1.5-kilometer (0.9-mile) long, narrow strip of waterfront along the Huangpu River in the city center, primarily composed of the riverside promenade and historic buildings of diverse architectural styles dating back a century. Featuring both retro and modern elements, and with its brilliantly illuminated and bustling night view being truly breathtaking, the Bund is regarded as the symbol of Shanghai and becomes one of Shanghai’s must-visit attractions.
The Bund Facts 
Our Tour Group at the Bund
  3-Day Private Shanghai Tour from $509
  1 Day Shanghai Highlights Tour from $109
More Shanghai Tours  Location: on the west bank of Huangpu River, stretches from the Waibaidu Bridge over the Suzhou River in the north to Yan’an East Road in the south. 
 Highlights: best night view in Shanghai; European style building clusters; perfect sightseeing spot along the waterfront
 Opening hours: it’s an all-year-round attraction and opens all day.
 Light opening hours: 19:00-23:00 from May to October, and 18:00-22:00 from November to April. During holidays such as New Year and National Holiday, or special events, the lights usually will be turned on earlier and turned off later.
 Time needed for sightseeing: 1-2 hours
History of the BundBefore Shanghai was opened as a trading port in 1843, the Bund was just a muddy and rudimentary riverbank. Later, in the mid-late 19th century, with the establishment of the British and French concessions, the infrastructure of the Bund gradually improved. Today, many Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical style architectural complexes in this area originated from the masterpieces of British architects and foreign investors. These buildings used to be residences of international renowned financial institutions such as banks, trading companies and insurance companies during the concession period, which stimulated the economic development of the Bund and even Shanghai. Therefore, this region is also known as the “Wall Street of the East”. In 1943, the Bund ended its centurial concession period and gradually welcomed new large-scale improvements and developments. It has not only retained its historical and cultural heritage but also incorporated modern elements, becoming an image of Shanghai and China’s economy, and also a popular tourist destination for visitors.
Best Time to Visit the BundThe best time to visit the Bund is in the early morning and at night. Strolling along the Bund in the early morning allows you to avoid the crowds and experience the genuine daily lifestyle of the local people; while visiting at night you will see a totally different version of the Bund that is bustling and embellished with golden neon lights. Lucky enough, you might even be able to witness a large-scale drone show. Night Views of the Bund 
Best Things to Do in the Bund
Joining Locals Doing Morning ExerciseElderly locals doing morning exercise have become a regular sight on the Bund. Here you can see them strolling, jogging, practicing Tai Chi or flying kites. Particularly, near the Huangpu Park, many energetic locals would wave the colorful dragon-shaped ribbons. Getting up early to join them is a delightful way to experience the authentic local way of life.
Strolling along the Waterfront Avenue and Admiring the Historical ArchitecturesThe Bund is renowned for its unique collection of international architecture. From the eclectic Asia Building (now China Pacific Insurance Co., Ltd.) in the south to the Former British Consulate General Building in the north, each building narrates a timeless story in its own distinctive style. As you stroll along the Bund, you’ll first be captivated by the grand exteriors of these row upon row of structures. And if you learn their stories, it feels like watching a long yet unforgettable classical film.
  Buildings No. 1 - No. 12 
  Buildings No. 13 - No. 20
  Buildings No. 23 - No. 33
  Pictures of the Bund Buildings 
Appreciating High Rises across the Huangpu RiverLooking across the Huangpu River, what catches your eye are high-rise buildings that are completely different from the Bund architectural complex and full of modern science and technology, including the Oriental Pearl Tower, the World Financial Center, Jinmao Tower and Shanghai Tower. These four buildings are the tallest skyscrapers in this city, dominating the skyline and forming an excellent backdrop for taking pictures on the Bund. Pudong Seen from the Bund Western-style Achitecture along the Bund  
Admiring the Sunset on Waibaidu BridgeWaibaidu Bridge, the first steel-framed bridge in China with a history of over a century, showcases the beauty of the industrial era. At sunset, the bridge’s unique triangular geometric structure, combined with the afterglow of the setting sun and the shimmering Suzhou Creek below, creates an excellent vantage point for you to take photos.
Dining at a Rooftop Restaurant of the BundThere are many open-air restaurants along the Bund, which are perfect places to enjoy delicious food while taking in the beautiful views of the Bund. For instance, the terraces of the Bund No.3, No.5 and No.6 offer various styles of dining options for you. Here, you can enjoy a romantic dining atmosphere and take some wonderful photos of the Bund and the modern skyline of Pudong Area.
Experiencing the Bund Sightseeing TunnelThe Bund Sightseeing Tunnel crosses the Huangpu River, connecting the Bund and the Lujiazui commercial district in Pudong New Area. This is the first cross-river sightseeing tunnel in China, integrating transportation and tourism functions. Inside the tunnel, different themed experience scenarios are set up through advanced technologies. Tourists can take the transparent sightseeing cable car and experience the futuristic tunnel while speeding across both banks of the Huangpu River at high speed. Sightseeing Maglev in the Sightseeing Tunnel East Nanjing Road  
How to Get to the Bund 
By MetroTake Line 2 or Line 10 and get off at East Nanjing Road Station. Then walk east along East Nanjing Road for about 10 minutes.
By Bus Monument to the People's Heroes 1.    Take City Sightseeing Bus Line 1, 3 or 5 to the Bund No. 13 Shanghai Customs House
2.    Take Bus No. 33, 55, 65, 123, 135, 576, 921, or 934, get off at Zhongshan East 1st Road-Nanjing East Road Station, then walk about three minutes along Zhongshan East 1st Road toward the riverside.
3.    Take Bus No.71 or 320 and get off at the Yan’an East Road Bund Station. Then walk east along Yan’an East Road for about 5 minutes and turn right at the intersection of Zhongshan East Road.

Shanghai Tower
 The Shanghai Tower, as China’s tallest and the world’s third tallest skyscraper, is located at Lujiazui, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. It serves as a monumental landmark in Shanghai, integrating commercial, office, hotel, exhibition, entertainment, and sightseeing functions. From the observation deck atop the tower, you can take in a panoramic view of the entire city—admiring the winding course of the Huangpu River, the retro architectural clusters of the Bund, and the towering high-rises in Lujiazui. With a total height of 632 meters, the tower consists of 127 above-ground floors and five underground levels. Its footprint covers 30,368 square meters, equivalent to the size of 4.5 standard football fields. The Night View around Shanghai Tower  
Exterior & Design Features Shanghai Tower The architectural structure of the Shanghai Tower is spiral-shaped, resembling a coiling dragon when viewed from a distance. This unique design, which breaks away from the monotonous form of traditional skyscrapers, not only stands out in architectural aesthetics but also boasts exceptional practicality. The gradually rotating structure significantly reduces wind resistance, ensuring the tower remains upright and stable even in strong winds. Additionally, the foundation consists of 955 piles, each reaching 86 meters in length, driven into the soft soil to securely support the tower’s weight of 800,000 tons—equivalent to the combined weight of 70 Eiffel Towers.
The building’s facade features a double-glazed curtain wall system to enhance its thermal insulation, heat resistance, and soundproofing performance. During the day, it reflects dazzling brilliance under sunlight, while at night, its lighting system activates, casting an array of colorful lights that create a stunning sightline for the entire Shanghai skyline. From a distance, you can be awestruck by its towering, luminous, and transparent structure; while inside the building, you can gaze at the magnificent cityscape through the fully transparent glass curtain wall.
Best Things to Do within Shanghai Tower
Experience the “Top of Shanghai” Sightseeing TourThe “Top of Shanghai” sightseeing tour starts from the Shanghai Tower Exhibition Hall on B1. The highlight of this hall lies in its status as a display space integrating culture, technology and architectural art. Through various high-tech display methods, visitors can gain an in-depth understanding of Shanghai’s urban development trajectory and the construction mysteries of the Shanghai Tower. On the B2, there are three ultra-high-speed elevators—OB1, OB2, and OB3—capable of reaching speeds of up to 20.5 meters per second. Taking these elevators allows visitors to reach the 118th floor, the Top of Shanghai Observatory Deck, in just 55 seconds. From the observation deck, you can overlook through the transparent glass curtain wall and take in the magnificent views of the entire Shanghai urban area. At sunset, you can experience the romance of the sunset’s afterglow.   Top of Shanghai Observatory Deck Ultra-high-speed Elevator of Shanghai Tower  
Appreciate the Light and Shadow Show of the Damper in the Tian Shi 632 Art SpaceThe Tian Shi 632 Art Space, renowned as the “world’s highest art space” located on 125-126 floors of Shanghai Tower, integrates music, light, projection, lasers, and other multi-dimensional artistic expressions to create an interactive experience for your senses. Between the two floors, there is the world’s only open damper exhibition area, equipped with technology driven interactive installations and artistic light shows, allowing visitors to fully appreciate the charm of this 1,000-Ton Tuned Mass Damper, known as the “Eye of Shanghai”. Shanghai Tower and Other Skyscrapers in Pudong
  More Pictures of Skyscrapers in Pudong New Area   
Enjoy a Leisurely “Book Café” Time in Duoyun Books on the 52th FloorDuoyun Books features unique visual design and tranquil reading space. Most importantly, the bookstore itself is free of charge. In addition, there are two observation decks in the north and south, which can be accessed unlimited times with a dining consumption receipt of the store. If you want to have a rest after sightseeing in crowded areas of this building, here is a perfect option. You can order a cup of coffee and dessert which costs about RMB 30-50, and enjoy reading or just sit near the observation deck with beautiful views, spending some leisure time.
Note: Duoyun Books requires advance reservation on the WeChat official account. The opening hours are 10:30-20:00 every Monday, and 10:00-20:00 from Tuesday to Sunday.  Duoyun Books Observation Deck of Duoyun Books  
Admire Ancient Chinese Artifacts in Shanghai Guanfu Museum on the 37th FloorShanghai Guanfu Museum has four permanent exhibition halls: the Porcelain Hall, the East-West Hall, the Goldware Hall, and the Sculpture Hall, as well as a temporary exhibition hall. The Porcelain Hall mainly features porcelain from different dynasties in northern and southern China, allowing you to appreciate the beauty of ancient Chinese porcelain craftsmanship. The East-West Hall displays over 100 exhibits, primarily export porcelain and furniture, showcasing the cultural exchange and fusion of craftsmanship between China and the West from the 16th to the 18th centuries. The Goldware Hall features over 200 exhibits, mainly ancient Chinese gold artifacts, supplemented by gold artifacts from China’s neighboring countries. The Sculpture Hall primarily displays 47 Buddhist statues from ancient China and neighboring countries.  If you are visiting the Shanghai Tower and happen to be interested in ancient Chinese artifacts, don’t miss this museum! 
  Shanghai Tower in Pudong  
Enjoy Fine Meal at Michelin Three-star Maison Lameloise on the 68th FloorYou are recommended to go to Maison Lameloise on the 68th floor, the first overseas branch of France’s famous century Michelin three-star restaurant, to experience the luxury food combining French cooking methods and fresh local ingredients from Shanghai. The business hours of this restaurant are from 11:30 to 13:30 from Friday to Sunday and from 18:00-20:30 daily. The best time to enjoy delicious food here is at dusk. You can book a seat by the window, which is perfect for taking photos with the backdrop of breathtaking scenery of sunset and city lights.

Shanghai Ferry
The Huangpu River running through Shanghai, divides the city into two parts - Pudong New District (east of the river) and Puxi Area (west of the river). The three islands of Chongming, Changxing, and Hengsha under the jurisdiction of Shanghai are separated from the main by the Yangtze River. As a result, ferries play a very important role in the city's transportation.  
Huangpu River Ferry 
As many bridges, tunnels, and subways are built, people have much more choices when traveling across the Huangpu River. However, ferryboats with 100-year's history are still popular choices for pedestrians and cyclists because of their convenience and low price. At present, there are in total 17 ferry lines serving nearly 40 ferry stations along both sides of the Huangpu River, providing links between Pudong and Puxi.
 Ticket Price:

Jing’an District, Shanghai
Jing’an District Facts
Chinese Name: 静安区 (jìng ān qū)
Population: 246,788
Area: 37 square kilometers (14 square miles)
Location: in the center of Shanghai, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200040
GDP (2018): CNY184.7 billion (USD 27.9 billion)
One of the Core Urban Areas
Jing’an District is located in the center of Shanghai, adjacent to Huangpu District and Hongkou District on the east, Changning District and Putuo District on the west and Xuhui District on the south. "Jing’an" is named after the Jing’an Temple, a must-see scenic spot in Shanghai. It is an important window for Shanghai's foreign exchanges and rewarded the best leisure tourism destination by China National Tourism in 2018.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Jing’an District
 Jing’an Temple
Jing’an Temple is a famous ancient temple in Shanghai. At present, the main buildings of the temple include the Shanmen (gate to the temple), Tianwang Hall, Daxiong Hall and Sansheng Hall. The silver Buddha enshrined in the Mahavira hall weighs as heavy as 15 tons. From a distance, the whole temple has a golden roof, particularly conspicuous. Jing’an Temple attracts many people to worship or visit. What’s more, the stunning and beautiful night view of the temple cannot be missed.
 Shanghai Natural History Museum
The Shanghai Natural History Museum displays tens of thousands of specimens. It has 5 floors and 10 permanent exhibitions, which are divided into three themes: natural evolution, life world and human civilization. What is most interesting is the skeleton of the 26-meter (85-feet) long Mamenchisaurus Sinocanadorum, the largest dinosaur in Asia with the longest neck in the world. The Exploration Center is children's favorite where they can experience the sense of achievement of digging fossils by themselves (Need an appointment in advance).
 Moller Villa
Moller Villa was a private garden villa owned by Moller, a wealthy Jewish businessman, and has transformed into Hengshan Moller Villa Hotel since 2005. The main building is a three-story house in Norwegian style. The interior decoration is very exquisite as beautiful and delicate patterns are carved everywhere. You can take photos in the hotel for free, or enjoy afternoon tea in the garden.
 Wujiang Road
With convenient transportation, Wujiang Road is a wonderful place for shopping, sightseeing and tasting delicious food. All kinds of special dishes and local snacks can be found there, among which the Xiaoyang Pan-Fried Bun Stuffed with Pork and Nanxiang Steamed Buns are the most famous.
 See more: 6 Best Food Streets in Shanghai 
Others: Jing’an Villa, Shanghai Exhibition Center
Best Time to Visit Jing’an DistrictThe best time to visit Jing’an District Shanghai is from September to November when the weather is clear and pleasing with the average temperatures of 21℃ (70℉). With dense buildings and a lack of green space, the city-centered Jing’an District is easy to form a heat island effect. So Jing’an District Shanghai has more hot days in summer from June to August and the average temperature is 28℃ (82℉). The winter time of Jing’an District, December to February, is about 7 ℃ (45℉). The rainy season in Shanghai starts in the middle of June every year and lasts for a month. It is not a good time to have a travel to Jing’an District during that time.

TransportationIt takes about 80 minutes from Shanghai Pudong International Airport by Metro Line 2 to Jing’an District Shanghai. Or visitors can take a flight to Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport and take Metro Line 2 to Jing’an District. Taking a bullet train is also available and visitors are able to reach Jing’an District Shanghai from Shanghai Railway Station in 35 minutes by Bus 927.
Metro Line 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 13 are serving in Jing’an District Shanghai. Visitors can take Metro Line 2 and 7 to Jing’an Temple and Metro Line 1, 2, 12 and 13 to Shanghai Natural History Museum. The starting price and charging standard of Shanghai taxis are different between day and night. It charges CNY 170-180 to Pudong Airport, CNY 50-60 to Hongqiao Airport and and CNY 20-30 to Shanghai Railway Station.

Shanghai Weather in March
 In March, spring weather warms up the whole city of Shanghai. Some drizzles fall, bringing the vibrant spring picture: the air is fresh and clean, trees like willows bud, flowers like cherry blossoms and tulips gradually bloom… Nice weather and bright spring scenery make March a definitely good month to visit Shanghai.
TemperatureAn overall increasing trend can be noticed throughout March. In the first half of the month, still a little cold days with the daily high and low of around 10-15 degrees Celsius (50-59 degrees Fahrenheit) and 5-10°C (41-50°F), respectively, are more common. In the second half month, warm days, which enjoy daytime temperature of around 15-25°C (59-77°F) and nighttime temperature of 10-15°C (50-59°F), show up more frequently.  Yu Garden in Cold March 
However, you cannot decide what to pack for your trip based only on the above overall temperature picture: instability is also an obvious feature of the temperature of Shanghai in March that cannot be overlooked. On the one hand, the temperature gap between day and night can be quite large, which may be over 15°C (27°F) sometimes. For instance, on March 2, 2025, the daytime was warm or even a bit hot at around 28°C (82°F), while the nighttime brought cold air with the temperature of only 10°C (50°F). On the other hand, temperature differences between two consecutive days can also be big, which are demonstrated by sudden temperature drops or rises of around 5-15°C (9-27°F).
Precipitation & HumidityAbout 14 rainy days show up in March on average, which is relatively frequent, but the average monthly precipitation is not high at only 84 mm. This indicates that drizzle is the main type of rain this month. What is also favorable for your trip is that drizzles usually stop quickly, followed by gentle sunshine. 
Shanghai suffers from wet and damp air in March, and the humidity is about 70% on average. You will feel even colder when the temperature is low, due to the high humidity.
 The Bund on Sunny Days Clear Sky in March  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursMarch in Shanghai gets gradually extending daytime from about 11.3 to 12.3 hours, so you don’t need to worry that you cannot gain enough daylight for walking around, and just slow down and have a leisurely trip, especially in the second half of the month. Besides, with relatively early sunset time at 17:51-18:12, you can enjoy illuminated night views early.
Plenty of sunshine guarantees good visibility and light conditions for outdoor visiting and photographing: sunshine hours per day average about 5 hours this month. During the midday hours of sunny days, when the UV index can reach 7, sun-protection measures are essential, especially for those having sensitive skin.

One of the Best Months to Visit ShanghaiMarch is considered one of the best months to visit Shanghai and trips to the Bund, the Yu Garden, the Nanjing Road, etc., will all reward you with perfect experiences:
1. Temperature-wise, Shanghai is gradually getting rid of the damp and chilly weather and becoming warmer and warmer, while sudden temperature drops take place only occasionally.
2. Rain, though a bit frequently, is usually light and short, guaranteeing plenty of sunshine.
3. The visitor volume is moderate this month, so you can book nice hotel rooms at budget-friendly prices and visit attractions at a leisurely pace without waiting in lines for a long period.
4. In March, Shanghai is ablaze with vibrant spring colors, as bright flowers bloom everywhere.  Disneyland Park Full of Flowers in March  
What to Wear in Shanghai in March 2027? Clothes: The weather of Shanghai in March is changeable, so you need to prepare clothes of different thicknesses. On most days in the first half of the month, and on some days in the second half of the month when Shanghai is hit by cold air, you should wear hoodies, thick sweatpants, and down jackets or wool coats. On most days in the second half month, you can change the down jackets or wool coats into 3-in-1 jackets or windbreakers. Sometimes, when the daytime temperature is over 25°C (77°F), even a trench coat or an outer layer of a 3-in-1 jacket alone is enough.
Shoes: Choose a pair of comfortable and relatively thick sneakers, walking shoes, or boots.
Others: 
1. Never forget to bring an umbrella with you when traveling to Shanghai in March.
2. Sun-protection items like sunglasses, hats, and sunscreen are better to prepare.
3. People who are allergic to pollen are advised to wear masks
Tips for Visiting Shanghai in March1. As mentioned above, March will not see very high visitor flow in Shanghai, and the Shanghai Disneyland Park also welcomes its rare slack season. You will indeed have a smoother trip that requires a relatively short time to queue; however, you should know that due to the decline in visitor numbers, the Park will close early, and the number of fireworks shows and parade performances will be reduced. If you plan to visit it this month, please check the related information in advance.
2. Try to arrange your travel on weekdays. In this month of flower blooming, weekends are the time for the locals to spring out, indicating that parks and public transportation will be crowded.
3. The climate of Shanghai in March is quite changeable, making it important to check the weather forecast from time to time. Shanghai Spring View 
4. Want to see flowers to feel the spring? Yu Garden provides pink cherry blossoms and white magnolias, and the area around the Oriental Pearl Tower has white magnolias and tulips to see. Or, if time permits, Gu Village Park, boasting 16,000 trees and a lively cherry blossom festival, and Jing’an Sculpture Park in the city center, with large-scale cherry blossoms and tulips, are recommended destinations to visit.
